title: CVE-2026-59346: Critical VMware Workstation and Fusion Flaw Enables Guest-to-Host Code Execution
content_md: Broadcom has addressed CVE-2026-59346, a critical integer-overflow vulnerability affecting VMware Workstation and VMware Fusion. The flaw carries a CVSS score of 9.3 and can allow an attacker with administrative privileges inside a virtual machine to cross the virtualization boundary and execute code on the underlying host. The issue resides in VMware’s VMXNET3 virtual network adapter implementation. Successful exploitation could turn compromise of an isolated guest operating system into compromise of the system hosting that virtual machine, significantly increasing the potential impact in development, research, testing, and enterprise virtualization environments. Broadcom released fixes in VMware Workstation 26H1u1 and VMware Fusion 26H1u1. The vulnerability affects the 25H2 and 26H1 branches of both products, and the vendor has not provided a workaround, making patching the primary remediation measure.
